key_insight: PI-MFA adds governing-equation and boundary-condition constraints to B-spline reconstruction so continuous flow fields stay smooth while also respecting physics.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a compact way to reconstruct CFD or experimental flow data for downstream analysis, differentiation, and visualization without losing physical consistency.
method: Tensor-product B-splines create compact, continuously differentiable flow-field approximations.
Control points are fit by optimizing data fidelity plus PDE residuals and initial/boundary-condition penalties.
Exact analytical spline derivatives are used to evaluate physics constraints efficiently.
evidence_signal: The paper reports tests on 1D convection-diffusion, 2D coupled Burgers, and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes cases, where PI-MFA reduced PDE residuals, improved balance-law consistency, and often lowered approximation error versus standard/regularized MFA.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the chosen physics model and constraint weighting, so inconsistent or incomplete PDE assumptions can bias the reconstruction.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed B-Spline Framework for Continuous Approximation of Flow Data
